title: Indexed BundleGraph reads reject task-dependency edges, disabling the ladybug backend
description:
LCLI-476 added task->task `dependency` edges to the projection. `readIndexedBundleGraph` (src/core/ladybug-driver.ts) selects authored edges with `WHERE n.kind <> 'task'`, which keeps `dependency` rows, then resolves both endpoints against the CONCEPT record-key map. A task record key is absent from that map, so every read corrupts with 'indexed edge is invalid'.

The sibling reader (readIndexedTraversalRecords, same file) filters on `edgeSourceKind(record) === 'concept' && edgeTargetKind(record) === 'concept'` before validating, which is why traversal survived and only the BundleGraph path broke -- `lore path`/`impact` stayed healthy while `graph`/`query`/`context` stopped using the index.

MEASURED, not inferred, on this repository 2026-09-14 (dev at 3d36293d, local CLI from the working tree):

  loadRetrievalGraph({ policy: 'indexed' }) -> throws
  'Ladybug projection verification failed: indexed edge is invalid'

  loadRetrievalGraph({}) -> backend 'reference', with
  'warning: native indexed retrieval failed; using the in-memory reference backend' on stderr

This repo's own Quest tracker carries 94 tasks with a non-empty `dependencies` array, so the trigger is ordinary, not exotic -- after LCLI-476 it is the normal shape of a Quest-backed workspace.

THE DEGRADATION IS WARNED, NOT SILENT. An earlier revision of this description claimed the opposite; see the correction note below for how that got in. The default `auto` policy catches the failure, prints the fallback warning, and returns a correct reference graph. What is wrong is that a shipped performance feature never engages, and that the warning names no cause (LCLI-498).

Found while implementing LCLI-477, which touches the same function.

acceptanceCriteria.text: readIndexedBundleGraph excludes non-concept-endpoint edges by the same declared predicate the traversal reader uses, not by a kind denylist
loadRetrievalGraph with policy indexed succeeds on a bundle whose tracker carries task dependencies
A regression test fails without the fix and is verified mutation-sensitive against it
The indexed and reference backends are asserted to agree on the edge set for a bundle carrying dependency edges

implementationNotes:
CORRECTION, 2026-09-14, before any of this landed: THE FALLBACK IS NOT SILENT. The description above says the failure is invisible. It is not. `loadRetrievalGraph`'s catch path already calls `warnReferenceFallback(..., "failed")`, so every affected command prints on stderr:

  warning: native indexed retrieval failed; using the in-memory reference backend

Verified by running `bun run src/cli.ts graph --plain` against this repo with the defect in place; the line is there, first on stderr, on every invocation.

HOW THE WRONG CLAIM GOT IN, because it is the more useful half: retrieval.ts's own docstring says "Failed indexed warnings and data are discarded" -- which is true of `indexedWarnings`, the warnings collected DURING the indexed attempt, and says nothing about the fallback notice. I read one sentence about one collector as a statement about the whole path and did not run the auto path before writing it down. The first command I ran in this session did print that warning; I piped it through `tail -5` and scrolled past my own evidence.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE, AND WHY THIS IS STILL A RELEASE BLOCKER: the indexed backend is dead on any Quest-backed workspace whose tracker carries a prerequisite, which after LCLI-476 is the ordinary case rather than an exotic one. This repository: 94 tasks with a non-empty `dependencies` array. A shipped performance feature that never engages is the defect, with or without a warning.

WHAT THE WARNING DOES NOT DO: it names no cause. "native indexed retrieval failed" is the same sentence for a corrupt edge, an unreadable generation and a version mismatch, so it cannot be acted on without a debugger. Filed separately as LCLI-498 rather than fixed here, because the obvious repair -- interpolating the cause -- would carry internal vocabulary ("Ladybug projection verification failed") into public output, which an existing test in indexed-retrieval.test.ts explicitly forbids. That needs a sanitised diagnosis, not a string concatenation.

FOUND BY ACCIDENT, WORTH RECORDING: nothing alerted anyone. It surfaced because LCLI-477 needed a working indexed path to verify its own indexed/reference fidelity, three hours after LCLI-476 introduced it. A reader who assumes a detector existed will not build one.

THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT MATTERS: `readIndexedTraversalRecords` filters on a declared endpoint-kind predicate before validating; `readIndexedBundleGraph` filtered on `kind <> 'task'`, a proxy for the same question. Two readers of the same table, one defensive by construction and one not -- so `lore path`/`impact` stayed healthy while `graph`/`query`/`context` stopped using the index. The fix adopts the traversal reader's predicate rather than extending the proxy.
